audit.title: Data Streams Tutorials

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Opens with filler — "Explore several tutorials to learn how to use the Data Streams" — not a self-contained answer. A one-sentence definition of Data Streams up top would make the intro liftable.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Strong for its size — 3 clean headings, 0 level skips, sections under 117 words, well-grouped bullets. A summary table (tutorial × network × SDK) would push this higher.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured facts show 0 numerals and vague quantifiers "several, various." No latencies, supported-chain counts, or SDK versions.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: 15 internal links, well-labeled and useful for routing; 0 external/primary sources. Appropriate for a hub, but no anchor to canonical spec/standard.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No crisp definition of "Chainlink Data Streams" or "Data Streams Aggregation Network" near first use — a missed liftable statement.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Measured facts confirm no JSON-LD, missing canonical, no datePublished/dateModified, no og/twitter tags. Note: raw `<head>` was not captured, so some tags may exist but couldn't be verified — the CLI should pass `<head>` for a full read.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code, and none is expected on an index page — treat as not applicable rather than a defect.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Covers "how do I fetch / stream / verify reports" through linked tutorials; no symptom- or error-phrased entry points and no troubleshooting.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming (Data Streams, DON, SDKs). No action needed.

audit.summary: This is a tutorial-index hub for Chainlink Data Streams — its GEO job is routing readers/agents to the right tutorial, not being cited as a standalone answer. Its biggest strength is clean, unambiguous structure with well-labeled internal links across Go/Rust/TypeScript SDKs and EVM/Solana verification paths. Its biggest opportunity is that the page carries **zero specifics, no canonical definition of "Data Streams," and no metadata** (no JSON-LD, canonical URL, or dates per Measured facts), so it neither gets cited itself nor establishes the entity for engines. Honest verdict: functional as human navigation, weak as a retrievable/liftable GEO asset — a few surgical additions would lift it materially.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical definition of Data Streams in the first liftable sentence
recommendations.where: Intro line, replacing "Explore several tutorials to learn how to use the Data Streams."
recommendations.issue: "Explore several tutorials to learn how to use the Data Streams."
recommendations.change: Lead with a self-contained definition, e.g. "Chainlink Data Streams delivers low-latency, on-demand market data from a Decentralized Oracle Network (DON), verifiable onchain. These tutorials show how to fetch, stream, and verify reports using the Go, Rust, or TypeScript SDKs." Keep the routing sentence after it.
recommendations.why: Gives engines a verbatim entity definition and a stand-alone opening chunk instead of filler.

recommendations.title: Add a summary table mapping tutorial → network → SDK/method
recommendations.where: Below the intro, spanning both "Fetch/Stream/Decode" and "Verify Reports" sections.
recommendations.issue: Reasons/decision factors are buried in prose bullets; 0 tables present.
recommendations.change: Add a table with columns Tutorial | Network (EVM / Solana) | Access method (SDK / REST / WebSocket / CPI) | Link, so an agent can pick the right path in one scan.
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract decision factors and build justified "which tutorial should I use" answers.

recommendations.title: Replace vague quantifiers and add concrete specifics
recommendations.where: Intro ("several tutorials") and NOTE block ("various programming languages").
recommendations.change: State the actual count ("five tutorials") and name the languages/networks explicitly (e.g. supported chains, SDK version numbers where known).
recommendations.why: Quantitative specifics are among the highest-lift changes; vague quantifiers underperform.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased sub-headings or an FAQ
recommendations.where: New short section or reworded H2s.
recommendations.issue: Headings are concept-titled ("Verify Reports"), not question-phrased.
recommendations.change: Add entries like "How do I verify a Data Streams report onchain?" and "How do I stream real-time reports over WebSocket?" linking to the relevant tutorials.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by task/symptom; question-phrased headings win retrieval that concept titles lose.

recommendations.title: Add page metadata: JSON-LD `TechArticle`/`CollectionPage`, canonical URL, last-updated
recommendations.issue: Measured facts show 0 JSON-LD blocks, missing canonical, no dateModified.
recommendations.change: Emit JSON-LD with `name`, `about: "Chainlink Data Streams"`, `inLanguage`, canonical URL, and a visible "Last updated" date.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and freshness signals raise parseability and E-E-A-T trust; likely a template fix, not per-page.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers: "several tutorials," "various programming languages" — replace with counts/names.
Filler opening sentence with no informational payload ("Explore several tutorials to learn how to use the Data Streams").
offPageNotes: Metadata absence is almost certainly a site-template issue (JSON-LD, canonical, dates) — fix once at the template level to benefit all hub pages.
The page already references `/llms.txt`, which is good site-level agent hygiene; ensure this hub is listed there as the canonical entry point for Data Streams tutorials.
Raw `<head>` was not captured; some meta/canonical tags may exist but are unverifiable here — pass `<head>` to the analyzer for a definitive read.
